jobs: draw a pivot table from the rows
group rows by one or two fields
aggregate a measure for each group
sort groups by aggregate, largest first
show a grand total under the table
summary: Reads the rows and the pivot choices held by the enclosing view and redraws the table in place, with a bar behind each aggregate scaled to the largest one. A missing or non-numeric measure counts as zero, and with no row group chosen the view shows a prompt instead of a table.

jobs: compute the aggregate value of a group
summary: Takes a group's sum, count, minimum and maximum and returns a copy with the value set to the chosen aggregate: average, count, minimum or maximum, with the sum as the default. An average over an empty group is zero.

jobs: tear down the table component
remove the view from the page
summary: Destroys the table component if one exists, ignoring any error the teardown throws, and then removes the view's root element from the page. The root element is removed even when no table was ever created.

jobs: define cell reference helpers for a spreadsheet reader
define colour and theme resolving helpers
define chart parsing and drawing helpers
define readers for font, fill and border styles
map connection type codes to their names
summary: Sets up the helpers the rest of the spreadsheet reader depends on: cell addresses, colours, rich text, chart markup and style records, along with the cap on pivot records and the connection type names. The part returns nothing itself, and the other parts of this unit call the helpers it defines.

jobs: strip an author name from a comment
resolve a relative package path
define the legacy colour palette
resolve a colour spec to hex
define the built-in number format codes
turn a spreadsheet date serial into a date
format a cell value as its format reads
summary: Continues the reader's setup with the comment author stripper, the relative path resolver, the legacy colour palette and the built-in number format codes, then defines the date serial conversion and the routines that apply a format code to a number or a date. The formatter returns the text a cell should show, rounded the way the workbook shows it, and the part itself returns nothing.

jobs: convert column widths and row heights to pixels
read a sheet's cells as row objects
profile what each column holds
resolve a cell's visible style
decide whether a conditional rule applies
build the drawn layout of a sheet
summary: Defines the helpers that turn a sheet into what it looks like: pixel conversions for column widths and row heights, reading cells as rows, profiling columns, resolving cell styles, testing conditional rules, and building the drawn layout with its notes and choice lists. A column is profiled by the kind that holds most of its non-empty cells, and a conditional rule that needs a formula is left unevaluated rather than guessed. The part returns nothing itself.

jobs: shift relative references in a formula
list every note in a workbook
place pictures and charts over cells
work out how far cell text spills
build the workbook's table views
read Power Query code from a workbook
count connected package parts
summary: Mostly defines helpers: reference shifting for formulas, the list of every note, picture and chart placement, the rule for how far cell text spills, the table view builders and the Power Query readers. The one routine written in full counts how many package parts exist and how many are connected, giving a percentage of zero when there are no parts.

jobs: publish the reader functions on the page
group the table views under one name
summary: Attaches the reader's functions, its table views and its helpers to the page as one shared object, so other scripts can call them by name. The object is only assigned here, and no reading happens until a caller uses one of its functions.

jobs: load the zip library on demand
summary: Returns the zip library if the page already has it. Otherwise it downloads the library once from a public CDN and returns that same copy on every later call.

jobs: convert a column number to letters
summary: Takes a zero-based column number and returns its spreadsheet letters, so 0 gives A, 25 gives Z and 26 gives AA.

jobs: read the column number from a cell address
summary: Takes a cell address such as AA5 and returns its zero-based column number, ignoring the row digits. Returns -1 when the address does not begin with column letters.

jobs: turn a cell range into bounds
summary: Takes a range such as A1:C3 and returns its top, bottom, left and right bounds, with rows counted from one and columns from zero, whichever corner was written first. Returns null when either end is missing or unreadable.

jobs: convert an ARGB colour code to hex
summary: Takes an eight-digit ARGB or six-digit RGB colour code and returns it as a lower-case hex colour, dropping the alpha byte. Any other text returns null.

jobs: split a list of cell references into ranges
summary: Takes a space-separated list of cell addresses and ranges and returns each as a range object, with a single cell becoming a one-cell range. Entries that cannot be read are dropped.

jobs: read the attributes of a colour element
summary: Reads the rgb, indexed, theme and tint attributes of a colour element into one record, with the numbers as numbers and tint defaulting to zero. Returns null when the element is missing or has none of the first three attributes.

jobs: join the text runs of a rich string
summary: Returns the text of a string element by concatenating its text runs in document order, skipping phonetic guide text. Returns an empty string when the element is missing.

jobs: read a number from a chart value
summary: Converts a value to a finite number, returning null for blanks and for anything that is not a number. Zero is a valid result, not a missing one.

jobs: read the text of a chart title
summary: Returns the text of a chart or axis title by joining its text runs, falling back to its stored value when it has no runs. Returns an empty string when the title holds neither.

jobs: read the colour of a drawing fill
summary: Reads the first colour inside a fill as an explicit value, a theme slot or a system colour's last value, with its modifiers as fractions. Returns null when the fill holds no colour.

jobs: convert an RGB colour to HSL
summary: Takes red, green and blue from 0 to 255 and returns hue in degrees with saturation and lightness from 0 to 1. A grey has no hue or saturation, so both come back as 0.

jobs: convert hue, saturation and lightness to RGB
summary: Takes a hue in degrees and saturation and lightness from 0 to 1 and returns red, green and blue from 0 to 255. The values are not rounded.

jobs: resolve a drawing colour to hex
apply shade, tint and luminance changes
summary: Turns a colour spec, either an explicit value or a theme slot, into a hex colour, applying shade, tint and luminance changes in that fixed order. Returns null when the spec is missing, its value is not a hex colour, or its theme slot is empty.

jobs: give each chart series its colours
set the chart's automatic colour list
summary: Sets the chart's automatic colours from the theme's accent slots, then gives each series a colour from its line for a line chart or from its fill otherwise, and gives each point its own colour from its fill. Returns the same chart object.

jobs: turn a chart part into a chart model
note unsupported chart features
summary: Reads chart markup into a plain model of the chart's title, type, legend, axes and series, and paints the series with the theme's colours when a theme is given. Returns null when the markup fails to parse or has no plot area, and records each unsupported feature, such as combined charts or date axes, so a caller can say what is missing.

jobs: read the settings of one chart axis
summary: Reads an axis's minimum, maximum, major unit, reversed direction, title and number format into a plain record. A logarithmic scale is recorded as unsupported on the chart.

jobs: read cached values of a chart series
summary: Reads the cached points of one series into an array placed by each point's index, with missing points as null, and returns the sheet reference and number format as well. A series that exceeds the preview limit is recorded as unsupported and returns no values.

jobs: read the settings of one chart series
summary: Reads a series' name, categories, values, fills, stroke, marker, line width and point colours into one record, using a numbered name, a default marker and a line width of three pixels where the chart leaves them out. A marker symbol the reader does not support is recorded as unsupported.

jobs: fill chart series from their sheet ranges
summary: Reads the category and value ranges each series points to in the workbook and replaces the cached values with them. A range that cannot be resolved is recorded as unsupported, and duplicate notes are removed from the list.

jobs: read a worksheet range as values
summary: Parses a sheet reference and returns the cell values of its range as numbers or as text. Returns null when the sheet is unknown, the reference is unreadable, the range spans both rows and columns, or it exceeds the point limit, and error cells or formulas without saved results are recorded as unsupported.

jobs: read a font's style from its element
summary: Reads the bold, italic, underline and strike flags, size, colour and face name of a font element. A missing or non-positive size becomes eleven points.

jobs: check whether a style flag is switched on
summary: Returns true when the named flag element is present and its value is absent, one or true. A flag written as zero or false is off, and an absent flag is off too.

jobs: read the colour of a cell fill
summary: Reads a pattern fill and returns its colour, or null for no fill and for the two default patterns that paint nothing. A differential fill takes its background colour first, and an ordinary solid fill takes its foreground colour first, falling back to the other one in each case.

jobs: read the four edges of a cell border
summary: Reads the top, right, bottom and left edges of a border element, each as a style and colour, with null for any edge that has no style or has the style none.

jobs: read one edge of a border
summary: Returns the style and colour of one named edge of a border, or null when the edge is absent or has no style or the style none.

jobs: read one value from a pivot cache
summary: Converts one cached value element into a value according to its type: text unescaped, numbers, dates and error codes as text, booleans as true or false, and blanks as null. Returns undefined for an element that holds no value.

jobs: read every part of a workbook package
collect the parts that are connected
join sheets to their names and positions
resolve shared string cell values
resolve chart data and colours
place each sheet's pictures and charts
summary: Walks every part of a workbook's XML and then resolves what the parts refer to, a step that waits until all parts are read so their order does not matter. It returns the element census and the connected parts, with sheet names, shared strings, chart data, colours and pictures joined to the sheets that use them.

jobs: attach comments to each sheet
set each sheet's visibility
join pivot tables to sheets and caches
join tables to their sheets
link each pivot cache to its records
resolve hyperlink targets from relationships
return the workbook reading result
summary: Finishes reading the workbook by attaching comments, visibility, pivot tables, tables and hyperlink targets to their sheets, and by linking each pivot cache to its records. A link the file does not declare is left as null rather than guessed, and the result holds the element census, the connected parts, the connections and the workbook model.

jobs: mark a package part as connected
record which sheets a part belongs to
summary: Marks a package part as connected through one kind of reference and records the sheets it applies to, or every sheet when told so. Once a part is marked for every sheet, a later mark for particular sheets does not narrow it.

jobs: parse one package part as XML
walk a part's element tree
build a chart model from a chart part
summary: Parses one package part and returns without effect if the XML is malformed. A chart part is also turned into a chart model and marked as used by every sheet, and then the whole element tree of the part is walked.

jobs: count each element by file and path
collect attribute values and text per element
pass each element to the connection recorder
summary: Visits an element and then each child in turn, counting each one by its file and path and collecting its attribute names with their values, and its text when it has no child elements. Each element is also handed to the routine that records what the workbook connects to.

jobs: note how a package part is connected
create a worksheet record on first sight
read each row's cells and formulas
read column widths and default sizes
read conditional formatting rules
start reading data validation entries
summary: For one element, records how its package part is connected, creates a worksheet record the first time a sheet is seen, and reads its rows and cells, column widths and default sizes, conditional formatting rules and the data validation entries up to their formulas. A cell's raw value comes from its value element, or from its inline text when there is no value element, and a cell's formula is kept as text or flagged as computed without stored text.

jobs: finish reading data validation formulas
note the sheet's drawing and comments links
read hyperlinks and the frozen pane position
count cells, styles and formulas per sheet
read merged cell ranges
read shared strings in position order
read number formats, cell formats and styles
summary: Continues reading one package part: it completes the data validation entries, notes each sheet's drawing and comments links, reads hyperlinks, the frozen pane, cell counts and merged ranges, then reads shared strings and the workbook's style tables. Every shared string is kept, even an empty one, so that later string positions still line up.
